name: Build-to-rent — detached
summary: Purpose-built single-family rental community of detached homes on one parcel, held by one owner, with private streets and an amenity package. Homes are smaller and simpler than for-sale product (a 2016 NAHB/Census profile shows a 1,500 SF median, mostly one story, fewer garages). Because the whole community is on-site, the baseline hard cost includes the horizontal infrastructure (streets, utilities, stormwater). Public cost data is thin: NAHB's community-level capitalization figure and two 2026 trade-guide estimates. The default is derived from production single-family costs plus horizontal infrastructure. Confidence is low-medium.

typicalSize.method: NAHB describes 'a typical development project with 200 units' (e1). Mid 150 reflects many 80–200 home communities; judgment.

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: NAHB analysis of 2016 Census microdata: SFBFR median 1,500 SF vs 2,419 SF for-sale (e4). That median includes attached product, so detached BTR is set slightly higher at 1,600 SF. The high end is still below the for-sale median of 2,216 SF (Census 2025). Judgment within those bounds.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Median SFBFR lot 6,200 SF (e4) ≈ 7 homes per net acre; ~10–20% is taken out for internal streets, amenity center and detention, and narrow-lot/cottage plans are allowed for at the high end.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Per e4, 40% of SFBFR homes had a two-car garage, 25% a one-car garage, and 35% no garage. Mid 2 counts the driveway/garage spaces typical of newer detached BTR.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Built up from vertical + horizontal. Vertical: production single-family per-SF ($145 mid, 2025$) less ~3–5% for rental-grade specs ≈ $140/SF × 1,600 SF ≈ $224k. Horizontal (in-community streets, utilities, stormwater, landscaping): ~$40k/home. That is consistent with $35k/door in a 2026 BTR townhome pro forma (e5) and with horizontal at '15–30% of total' (e3). Amenity area flatwork/landscape ~$6k/home. Total ≈ $270k. Low ≈ 1,300 SF × $115 + $25k ≈ $175k; high ≈ 1,900 SF × $185 + $60k ≈ $410k. Checks: the 2026 guide's vertical-only $180k–$350k per home (e2) brackets the vertical portion. NAHB's $60M per 200 units = $300k (e1) is capitalization 'to cover construction costs' and likely includes soft and financing, consistent with ~$270k hard. Labeled 2026$ (the newest evidence is 2026; the single-family baseline is 2025$).

perSF.method: = perPrimaryUnit / sfPerPrimaryUnit (incl. the per-home share of horizontal infrastructure): 175k/1,300, 270k/1,600, 410k/1,900.

scope.notes: Homes plus all in-community horizontal work (private streets, water/sewer/storm, dry utilities, grading, landscaping, fencing) incl. GC general conditions and OH&P. Excludes the clubhouse/pool amenity package (separate line item), land, off-site improvements, impact/tap fees, soft costs and FF&E.

qualityTiers.method: Economy ≈ low/mid per-SF (135/169). Premium/luxury are judgment; BTR finishes cluster near standard because of durability-driven spec sheets.

systemSplit.method: The single-family split (NAHB 2024 Table 1 mapped to CSI) is scaled to ~85% for the vertical home. The remaining ~15% horizontal share (e3: '15–30% of total'; ~$40k of $270k) goes to 31 (grading), 32 (streets, paving, landscape, fencing) and 33 (wet and dry utilities). Div 11 stays at ~2% because BTR homes include a washer/dryer and refrigerator.

lineItems.name: In-community horizontal infrastructure (streets, utilities, stormwater) per home

cost.method: Mid ≈ the $35k/door horizontal in a 2026 BTR pro forma (e5), raised for the longer street frontage per detached home. Range = 15–30% of a $175k–$410k hard cost (e3).

lineItems.notes: Carve-out of the hard cost; shown separately because it varies most by site.

lineItems.name: Amenity center: clubhouse/leasing office, pool, dog park, trails

cost.method: The 2026 guide names clubhouse, pool, dog park and trails as standard amenities that 'add cost' but gives no figures (e2). Judgment: 2,000–4,000 SF clubhouse/leasing at ~$300/SF + pool deck ~$400–800k + dog park, mail kiosk, trails ~$200–500k.

lineItems.notes: Added on top of the per-home hard cost; ~$13k/home at 150 homes.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Judgment: window coverings, smart-home locks/thermostat kits and the clubhouse furniture share. Major appliances are in the hard cost.

pctOfHard.method: A 2026 BTR pro forma carries soft costs at 13% of hard cost, plus carry/interest reserve at 5.5% of total project cost (e5). Mid 17% ≈ 13% + ~4% for financing fees and lease-up marketing. No for-sale commissions. High = entitlement-heavy jurisdictions.

softCosts.notes: Lease-up costs and an operating deficit reserve are often carried as soft costs in BTR underwriting.

hard.method: A 2026 BTR townhome pro forma carries 8% of hard cost (e5); mid set slightly lower for repeat detached product. Low/high is judgment.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Low hard $175k × 1.12 ≈ $195k; high $410k × 1.24 + amenity share ≈ $525k, rounded up. NAHB's $300k/unit construction capitalization (e1) sits inside.

evidence.quote: A typical development project with 200 units requires a total capitalization of $60 million to cover construction costs.
evidence.scopeNotes: Value computed by the researcher: $60M / 200 units. An advocacy round number; scope (land, soft, financing) is not defined. The page also notes ~62,000 built-for-rent starts over the last four quarters, down 26%.

evidence.quote: BTR homes typically cost $180,000 to $350,000 per home to build, before land.
evidence.scopeNotes: Trade cost guide, 2026; covers vertical construction only. Community-size totals table (vertical, excl. land and horizontal): 26–50 homes $5M–$17M; 51–100+ homes $10M–$35M+.
Refers to horizontal costs (roads, grading, utilities, stormwater). Trade guide; low confidence.

source.title: Contrasting Built-for-Rent and For-Sale New Single-Family Homes

evidence.quote: The median square footage of SFBFR homes in 2016 was 1,500 square feet
evidence.scopeNotes: From 2016 Census SOC microdata. Also: 77% of SFBFR were townhouses/attached; median lot 6,200 SF vs 8,500 for-sale; 61% one story; 35% no garage. The data is old; BTR detached product has grown since.

evidence.quote: Horizontal/site (lot development and infrastructure) $1.68M [$35K per door]; Vertical hard costs $10.69M ($165/SF); Soft costs (13% of hard cost); Contingency (8% of hard cost)
evidence.scopeNotes: Illustrative 48-unit BTR townhome pro forma (May 2026), not an actual project. Sun Belt is mapped to regionKey US because no specific market is named.

openQuestions: No audited BTR community budget found. Public REIT development disclosures (e.g., AMH development program per-home investment) or municipal PID/TIRZ documents for BTR communities would give direct per-home figures.
The amenity package cost is a judgment.
NAHB's 2016 SFBFR profile is old; a newer Census microdata cut for detached BTR size would improve sizing.
